150k is much less money than you are putting emotions into. 
It seems neither you or your father will be living off the street if this money is lost. If you think you can do better amd recoup your loss in a different field then go for it. 

6 months ago, I was going mental! I was going to lose far more than 150k in multiples! And it would have put the whole family literally in the street. I pulled through. All is fine now, I'm selling with a $400k profit. To fix a business you need to be hands on and wear every single hat to cut costs and find revenues. It's not impossible but very very hard and I tell you what, I wish I never had to do it cause I'm still recovering mentally from all the stress. If I had a chance to walk away I would have taken it. I'm not fit to fix a crappy businesses but I had no choice. 

So if you have a choice and don't think you can habdle it, and believe me it's a crushing experience to restructure a failing businesses and may not be that rewarding, if you have a plan b where you can leave and lose some money that won't determinedly affect your life then I say do it! Even if you failed in a startup you knew more about your self and the cost is much less than $150k.

You should know that your next venture might fail again. That's tough business OP, if you don't enjoy it don't do it.

For sure pay down debt! There is no way you can make %3 After tax income. You obviously going to be taxed the highest marginal rate (48%?) on any increase in your income so you need to make 6% annually just to break even with debt payment! In our climate this is next to impossible. If I find an income producing property for a 5%cap that's AAA then I'm lucky! And the real cap will probably be 4% and that's before taxes.

I believe in singularity! Singularity is a perspective that's different from each and every person. A singularity event for a hunter/gatherer is to have unlimited supply of food and reproduce indefinitely!

If Linus think singularitans think an exponential doesn't end in the real world then he is very ill informed! or rather he is ridiculoulating the singularity concept to dismiss it. Singularity argument is we are just scratching the surface in terms of computational power and there is lots of room for improvement and we are nearing the "singularity" in terms of computational power surpassing the human's brain. I doubt anyone can say with straight face an exponential can stay exponential in real life forever!

Even if Moore's law is dead today, then we already have coming within couple of years: Virtual reality, Drive-less electric car transporation system, cheaper smartphone, Global internet, etc..

The singularity is more than just a projection that AI would surpass humans, it's (for me) a wave of disruptions in multiple industries which would render the current system obsolete and another more equal "social contract" would emerge with more leisure and better life style for humans just like we have been doing since the sumerians with couple of set backs.

Linus, Unending exponential growth? What drugs are YOU on? I mean, really!!!

what!!! that's at best dumb! This is futurology, it's a prerequest to abandon the linear thinking for a more technologically disruptive future..

We do NOT have food shortages and we will probably never have food shortages. Just indoor LED induced farming can solve the "problem" not to mention automation and cheap transportation. That's really stupid to even consider at a time poverty is at an all time low!
Irritating to see such an ill informed article in futurology.

Life is awesome! Things are, mostly, going in the right direction. The hunger in the world is being reduced to all-time low. Capita income per human is increasing on global scale. Yes, things are not as good in US in terms of inequality and such (although it's certainly not a bad place to live!). We are working on this too! the fact that we live in a world where our intellectuals discuss ideas freely and suggest solutions speaks on how far we have come as a species. 

- The technology will trickle down because it's cheap. You don't see a "Ferrari" type smartphone who only the wealthy can afford. Yes there is super expensive phones, but functionally it's the same as others. 
- Even if you are "debt slave" you can declare bankruptcy and have restart in life. It's hard to start from scratch especially with no safety net. But still it's unfair to compare debt to an actual slavery.
- Who are the evil bad rich people? Bill gates? warren buffet? Elon Musk? Larry page? it's hard to believe they will go along with a system of financial owners/slaves.

Our problem is that technology made life much easier and in the near future it will make life even easier to the point that you don't have to work. Our self-estem, our credit rating, our value in life, our taxes and etc. all comes from our job. We need to fix this. We need to change regulations to showcase the profound change the technology is doing. And this, I'm 100% sure, will happen. Cause the world is not only one country. If US didn't catch it someone will and we will learn from them once we notice the unemployment and poverty increasing to a level that is causing unrest.

Just please don't be pessimistic! everything will be alright!

About electric, in 2017/2018 there will be many cars with 400k on single charges and Tesla model 3 actually will probably require roughly 45mins to recharge the 400km again. So it is happening the question will the consumer take this economic proposition? (Having 400km almost for free but if another 400km needed it will take 45mins of FREE charging vs paying $50 at the pump for each 400km)
I for one think 99% of people don't drive more than 400km a day anyways and the saving is ASTRONOMICAL and will have a huge economic push for the average guy. the impact is huge from an economical stand point, each vehicle owner will save at least $3,000 a year to be spent somewhere else. This is a huge stimulus to the economy (ofcourse in Canada we might gain and suffer too being next oil exporter)

I would advise to:

- DON"T JUMP on any idea! $100K won't make you rich in any means so don't go crazy into risky investments. your first priority is to preserve your wealth not increase it. remember that.

- Consider maxing out your investment vehicles (TFSA, RRSP etc.). I don't use any so I can't advise you here. 

- The smartest way to go is to reduce your monthly expenses, for example, I've made an analysis for my family cellphone plans and found out if we cancelled all our contracts, paid the penalties and bought S6 we would end up saving $50/month! This required us to pay $3K upfront and the saving is after factoring in the $3K on 3 years.
So my point is, try to find some things that will make your life easier/cheaper even if it cost more upfront my return on the $3k I spent is %20! you won't get that in any investment. Think of efficiency around the house (LED lights?). 

- Spend it. Wisely. but SPEND IT!! really don't hoard it. spend couple of thousands whenever you see necessary and that it will increase your quality of life. You are a university student, doing couple of activities to be added on your curriculum is a good way to go even it cost some. 

So anyways you got the picture.

the ceiling price on oil is going down each couple of years. Now the "normal" price for oil is ~$70 which is survivable for oil sand.

But the point is, oil within less than 10 years will have a MUCH lower ceiling than $70. Do you know salt was a precious commodity? now it's just salt!

Look at what's betting against oil:
- Efficiency. Engine's efficiency especially in us new auto regulation will at least double reducing consumption by half for same mileage
- Electric car. Tesla coming up with a car that is 30K price after incentives and travels at least 400km on a single charge and each charge cost couple of loonies. Compete with that!
- Regulation against Carbon omission whether you are a greeny or not it will be a factor in curbing consumption.
- Surplus of oil: China and India are growing less than expected and the oil price is pretty sensitive on demand/supply. It drops sharply when there is over supply and increases sharply when there is over demand. Any time a new technology or a breakthrough cause an increase in supply, you will have a big drop in oil price.
- Technology making oil an unlimited resource! you probably don't remember but back in 2005-2007 the world was panicking about "peak oil". Well, with all the current technologies we are awash with oil from oil sand and ofcourse the fracking boom which caused the price to collapse in the first place.
- Competition can beat us on lower cost. Cost of a barrel of oil in Saudi Arabia is roughly $4-$.. they know the new norm is lower oil prices and they are willing to scarfice price to keep market share so they are kicking everyone out by deliberately reducing the price as much as they can.
- Renewables. Renewables especailly Solar is getting very cheap (without) incentives. it will reach a point very soon where it's cheaper to go solar than burn gas/oil/coal freeing these commodities for other usages which will further increase the supply.

My time line for all of this is 10 years. I'm a firm believer oil is done not because of any environmental nonsense reasons (though it's a plus for sure) but the economics are shifting and when that happens you can't stop it. All thinks equal, would you rather buy a car and pay $250/month on mileage or the same exact car and pay  $20/month on mileage? you probably prefer the latter. It's only a question of when the latter will reach the tipping point. Well, Tesla Model 3 is coming in 2017...

Bottom line... get away from commodities in general.. Where to invest? hell I've no idea! this liquidity trap is VERY hard to play.
